register.name: International bank financing with an African Development Fund guarantee
register.detail: Closed 18 September 2026 · 12-year final maturity · African Development Fund partial credit guarantee · Second-loss insurance from the IsDB Group’s insurance subsidiary
register.text: A €500 million loan from international banks to the Republic of Benin, backed by a partial credit guarantee from the African Development Fund. It finances education, health, access to water, infrastructure, renewable energy, agriculture and jobs for young people and women: six of the seven standards in one loan.

register.name: Inaugural international sukuk
register.detail: Issued 22 January 2026 · 7 years · Coupon of 4.92% in euros after a dollar-euro hedge of the full amount
register.note: The first inaugural international sukuk by an African State, in the Ministry’s words
register.text: Benin’s first sukuk, Islamic finance certificates sold to international investors, with a seven-year maturity. A simultaneous dollar-euro hedge of the full amount gives it a coupon of 4.92% in euros.

register.name: Dogo-Bis Multipurpose Dam, Phase 1
register.text: Phase 1 of a dam programme with an overall envelope of $580 million.

register.name: Alafia 1, Feeding Benin for the Future
register.text: Nutrition, health and early childhood services for women and children: $150 million from IDA and $20 million from the Global Financing Facility.

register.name: Extended Fund Facility and Extended Credit Facility
register.detail: Approved July 2022 · Seventh and final review completed 25 February 2026 · SDR 484 million in all
register.note: About $36.3 million of it released on the final review
register.text: Benin’s IMF-supported programme of 2022 to 2026, completed with its seventh and final review. Over the programme the fiscal deficit fell to 3.1% of GDP in 2024, and the IMF revised central government debt to 60.5% of GDP at end-2024.

register.name: Resilience and Sustainability Facility
register.detail: Approved December 2023 · Fourth and final review completed 25 February 2026 · SDR 148.6 million in all
register.note: About $81.6 million of it released on the final review
register.text: The IMF’s long-term financing for reforms that build resilience to climate change, completed with its fourth and final review. Climate resilience protects the harvests, water and homes behind the seven standards.

register.name: Women entrepreneurs (WEDAF)
register.text: Access to finance and growth for women entrepreneurs in the formal and informal sectors.

register.name: Godomey–Ouidah–Hillacondji road upgrade
register.detail: Signed 12 October 2026, Bangkok · IsDB co-financing · Total cost €576.06 million
register.text: Financing to expand and upgrade the road from Godomey through Ouidah to Hillacondji, to improve road safety, cut travel times and transport costs, and strengthen trade along the Abidjan–Lagos corridor. Cheaper transport serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Legume-based farming for soil fertility and food security
register.detail: Signed 12 October 2026, Bangkok · IsDB co-financing · Total cost €20.70 million · Five development poles
register.note: Soil fertility, food security and climate resilience
register.text: Financing to spread legume-based farming, improve soil fertility, strengthen food security and build climate resilience across five development poles. It serves the food standard, where 65.6% of Beninese are moderately or severely food insecure.

register.name: West Africa gas market development
register.detail: IDA · Approved 29 June 2026 · With Côte d’Ivoire and Togo
register.text: Benin’s share of a $140 million regional project to build national gas markets and shared supply.

register.name: Gulf of Guinea Northern Regions Social Cohesion (COSO), additional financing
register.detail: IDA · Approved 25 June 2026 · With Côte d’Ivoire and Togo
register.note: Total for Benin, Côte d’Ivoire and Togo
register.text: Additional financing for community investments, infrastructure, livelihood support and inclusion in the northern regions of the three countries. In Benin, 595 community subprojects have been completed, benefiting over 679,000 people.

register.name: Regional DARES, distributed renewable energy, phase 1
register.detail: Approved 22 June 2026 · With the Central African Republic, Liberia and Sierra Leone · First phase of an $853 million programme
register.text: Solar home systems, mini-grids and other off-grid technologies for rural and remote communities. It serves the energy standard, the furthest from reach in Benin.

register.name: Grand Nokoué solid waste
register.detail: Approved 25 March 2026 · Sovereign loan · Up to 18 years · Parallel EIB loan of €35.5 million
register.note: Half of a €71 million programme; the second EBRD project signed in Benin
register.text: A sovereign loan to modernise solid waste management in the Grand Nokoué region, home to about 2.8 million people, with sorting centres, composting plants and landfill upgrades. Clean, safe neighbourhoods serve the shelter standard.

register.name: West Africa Coastal Areas (WACA+), Phase 1
register.detail: IDA, PROBLUE and private capital · Approved 17 March 2026 · With Mauritania
register.text: Coastal protection and blue economy jobs at the Bouche du Roy estuary and the mouth of the Mono river.

register.name: Western Africa Regional Digital Integration Program, second operation (WARDIP2)
register.detail: IDA · Approved 10 March 2026 · With Liberia and Sierra Leone
register.note: Total for Benin, Liberia and Sierra Leone
register.text: Upgraded digital infrastructure, a more business-friendly environment and help for businesses to scale across regional markets. It serves the livelihood standard through jobs and trade.

register.name: Rural electrification in Mono, Couffo and Borgou
register.detail: Signed 2025 · Sovereign loan for SBEE · Part of a €173 million programme with AFD, the EIB and an EU grant
register.note: The EBRD’s first financing in sub-Saharan Africa
register.text: Extends and modernises medium- and low-voltage networks to connect 120,000 new households, about 600,000 people, in 750 rural villages and towns. It serves the energy standard, the furthest from reach in Benin.

register.name: Clean Oceans Initiative, Grand Nokoué
register.detail: Approved 11 December 2024 · Signed 23 December 2024 · Total cost about €71 million
register.note: Parallel to the EBRD loan for the same programme
register.text: Financing to modernise solid waste management in the five municipalities of Grand Nokoué: sorting units at 60 collection points, four sorting centres, four composting units, a biogas unit and the securing of two landfills, with a focus on plastic waste. Cleaner, safer neighbourhoods serve the shelter standard.
